newsitem.title: USA: Charges of neglect dismissed against Danish mother.
newsitem.headline: Charges of neglect dismissed against Danish mother.

text.p: Charges of neglect were dismissed on Wednesday against a Danish mother who parked her baby in a stroller outside a New York City restaurant -- on the condition that she leave the United States by next week.

Danish actress Annette Sorensen appeared at a brief hearing before Judge Sheldon Rand in Manhattan Family Court, where the judge and officials with the city's Administration of Children's Services agreed to drop the so-called petition of neglect.
However, lawyers for the 30-year-old Sorensen must return to court next Wednesday and prove that she has left the country.
She has said she has a plane ticket to go home to Copenhagen on Tuesday.
Sorensen's case sparked trans-Atlantic debate after she was put in jail on May 10 for two days and her 14-month-old baby put into foster care for four days.
Sorensen, 30, and the baby's American father, Exavier Wardlaw, had left the baby outside an East Village restaurant while they were having a drink and watching her through the window, police said.
Passers-by, who said 14-month-old Liv was cold and crying, called police.

The mother's attorneys said Sorensen did not think twice about leaving the child outside the restaurant because it was common practice in Copenhagen. But here, city officials questioned the wisdom of being so trusting in New York.
A criminal charge of endangering the welfare of a child was dismissed last week against Sorensen. The neglect charge was filed separately in family court.

Neglect charges also were dismissed on Wednesday against the baby's father, who lives in New York City. However, he still faces criminal charges of endangering the welfare of a child and disorderly conduct and is due back in Criminal Court on June 4.
